title: Context Management: Budgeted Windows
objective: After this lesson you will be able to allocate token budgets per context section, truncate by value priority, place summarization checkpoints, and prove fit on longest gold conversations.
why: Context is the scarcest agent resource: every token costs money and attention, and overflow truncates silently (usually the system prompt's tail — your most important rules). Budgeted windows allocate per section (system/contracts/examples/history/tools), truncate low-value first, and summarize at thresholds — fit by design on the longest real conversations, never hoped on average ones.

blocks.text: Split the window: **system/contracts** (protected, never truncated), **examples** (capped count), **retrieved context** (top-k bounded), **history** (shrinking first), **tools/output scratch** (bounded). Priority order defines truncation sequence: history trims before examples, examples before contracts. Unbudgeted context spends randomly — budgeted spends deliberately.

blocks.caption: Priority-ordered packing: protection by rank, truncation from the bottom

blocks.text: At thresholds (history > N tokens), a **summarizer** compresses older turns into a rolling digest (decisions, open items, key facts — never verbatim needs), replacing bulk with density. Checkpoints trigger on size, run on schedule (not every turn — cost), and preserve open loops explicitly (summaries that drop pending items corrupt downstream). Digest quality is itself gold-tested.

Budgets validate against **longest gold conversations**, not averages: assemble worst-case contexts and assert fit with headroom. Overflow handling is specified (what truncates first is policy, documented), never discovered (silent system-prompt tail loss). Fit proven on extremes holds everywhere below.

blocks.title: Pack the window
blocks.note: Run it: expect system,contracts,examples kept (2400) with history TRUNCATED. Priority protects contracts while history — lowest value density — absorbs the cut. Budgets direct truncation, never hope.

items: Budget per section with priority ranks: contracts protected, history truncated first
Summarization checkpoints at size thresholds preserve decisions + open loops, never verbatim bulk
Prove fit on longest gold conversations; truncation order is documented policy

exercise.prompt: (a) Run the practice packer and confirm which section truncates. (b) Raise history priority above examples and re-run; state what the inversion risks. (c) Write the summarization trigger rule (threshold + what the digest must preserve) for a support agent.
hints: Baseline: system+contracts+examples kept (2400/3000), history truncated. Priority protects value density.
Inverted: examples truncate while verbose history survives — contracts still safe (priority 90), but demonstration quality dies for chatter.
Trigger: history > 2000 tokens → digest (decisions, open items, key facts); verbatim recent 5 turns kept; open loops explicitly preserved.
exercise.why: Priority inversion experiments prove ranks have consequences: protection follows value density deliberately. Trigger design (threshold + preserved content) makes summarization a policy, not a hope.
exercise.code: // Budget-tune pattern: reorder priorities, observe truncation, justify ranks.

quiz.q: Overflow truncates silently — most likely victim and fix?
options: System-prompt tail (most important rules): priority budgets protecting contracts + proven fit on longest conversations
quiz.explain: Silent truncation hits whatever overflows — usually trailing system rules. Priority protection plus worst-case proof prevents it structurally.

quiz.q: Summarizer drops open loops. Consequence + fix?
options: Downstream acts on closed assumptions: digests must explicitly preserve open items + decisions; gold-test digest quality
quiz.explain: Summaries that lose pending work corrupt downstream reasoning. Open-loop preservation is a digest requirement, tested like any contract.

quiz.q: Validate budgets against averages or extremes?
options: Longest gold conversations: fit proven at extremes holds everywhere below; averages hide the overflow cases
quiz.explain: Overflow lives at extremes by definition. Worst-case proof with headroom is the only validation that prevents silent truncation.

summary: Priority budgets, value-ordered truncation, scheduled summarization preserving open loops, worst-case proof. Windows managed, never hoped.
